native_result.query: How were the phases of the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) characterized in terms of the first principal component in a PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices?
native_result.HypoA: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In a PCA on the twelve forms of capital (hatchets/swords, daggers, house size, copper/gold, amber, monument count, hoards/deposits, sickles, axes/celts, monument size, pottery form, pottery decoration) computed in hundred-year time slices, PC1 (≈30% of variance; a capital/complexity gradient led by copper/gold, pottery decoration, hoards, hatchets/swords and daggers) places both the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) at the NEGATIVE (low) pole. The Middle Neolithic is the most negative of the Neolithic (mean ≈ -1.4, trough ≈ -1.8 around 3200-3000 BCE); the Younger Neolithic is also negative on average (mean ≈ -1.1) but less extreme and rising/recovering across the period (≈ -1.6 at 2900 BCE toward ≈ -0.4 at 2300 BCE). Thus the Middle Neolithic is the lower/more-negative phase and the Younger Neolithic, still below zero, trends upward toward it. Positive PC1 (high capital/complexity) only emerges later (Late Neolithic ~1900 BCE, especially the Bronze Age). The absolute PC1 sign is a convention (fixed so the Bronze Age is positive); the MN-vs-YN relative comparison is sign-invariant.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded data/capital.csv (decimal=','); 39 rows = one 100-year bin each, 4300-500 BCE, 12 Z-scored forms of capital; 0 missing, 0 duplicate BCE. Verified capital.csv == time_series_data.csv *_inter at century marks. 2) Defined periods from the 'group' column: MN={3400..3000} (3400-3000 BCE, 5 bins), SG/YN={2900..2300} (2900-2300 BCE, 7 bins) — matches the question. Binning convention: each row labels a 100-y bin by its older/start year; period assignment comes from the group labels so the within-bin boundary convention does not matter. 3) Standardized each of the 12 variables to mean 0/std 1 (ddof=1) -> PCA on the correlation matrix via SVD (numpy). 4) Fixed PC1 sign toward greater capital/complexity: flipped so the mean PC1 of the Bronze Age bins (OBA+YBA) is positive; documented that absolute sign is a convention and the relative comparison is sign-invariant. 5) Extracted PC1 scores per bin; compared MN vs YN in mean, range (min/max) and within-period linear trend; reported explained variance and PC1 loadings. 6) Context: pollen landscape-openness PC1 (MEAN / SMOOTH_MEAN_100y) for both periods. 7) Robustness: aggregated the 12 forms into assumed conceptual capital groups (economic/social/cultural/symbolic/domestic), PCA on group means, compared MN vs YN. Script: analysis_pca_capital.py (re-run reproduces all figures).
